briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin today's climate briefing for September 21, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of the Climate Crisis and its Comprehensive Impacts
sections.content: According to the annual report released by scientists today, 7 out of the 9 'planetary boundaries' essential for Earth's life prosperity have been transgressed to unprecedented levels, warning that the Earth's life-support systems have deteriorated to their worst on record [133]. Amidst this global crisis, the ongoing El Niño phenomenon has already broken previous records, showing a record temperature increase of 3.05C in the central Pacific months before its anticipated peak [134]. The impacts of climate change are already intensifying worldwide, with Bangladesh suffering from sweltering heat [1], and marine ecosystems being disrupted, such as tidal range changes of approximately 20cm in the West Sea over 30 years [2], and even unusual phenomena like the appearance of bluntnose sixgill sharks in Busan's North Port [25]. Furthermore, turbulence observations have increased sevenfold over the past five years, threatening air passenger safety [16], and despite deaths from record-breaking heatwaves, movements denying the climate change crisis have been observed in the international community [123]. This climate crisis is leading to increased financial losses [14] and a surge in climate litigation [17], issuing a warning about 'climate responsibility' for corporations and governments [9].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Climate Change Response Efforts and Carbon Neutrality Practices
sections.content: Even amidst the deepening climate crisis, various efforts are underway domestically and internationally to achieve carbon neutrality. Positive signs include a 0.9% decrease in total domestic greenhouse gas emissions [8]. The adaptability of the fisheries sector is being enhanced through the development of climate-resilient aquaculture species, such as Gunsan City's pilot oyster farming [3] and Jeonbuk Self-Governing Province's initiation of seaweed farming research [7, 10, 19]. Furthermore, ecosystem-based adaptation efforts are active, with Seongdong-gu developing low-maintenance gardens resilient to climate change [13, 20], and Lotte Chemical pursuing seagrass bed restoration in Geumodo [30, 68, 75]. Anyang City [22] and Suwon Special City [33, 37, 45, 50, 55, 60, 66, 76, 80] are encouraging carbon neutrality practices by operating life-cycle-specific climate crisis response education for citizens, and Gimhae City has achieved recognition as an excellent institution for its citizen-participatory carbon neutrality policies [32, 36, 46, 64, 69]. Alongside these, voluntary community-led carbon neutrality campaigns, such as those by the Yeongjong Family Volunteer Group [56, 73] and Seongbuk Donam 2-dong Residents' Autonomy Committee [77, 81], are also consistently being carried out [27, 51, 79].

sections.title: 🌍 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Current Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy, a core pillar of carbon neutrality, is accelerating both domestically and internationally. Five major domestic power generation companies plan to quadruple their renewable energy generation by 2030 [82], and Jeju Province is expanding 100% renewable energy certification in the livestock sector to include Hanwoo (Korean native cattle) [89, 91, 93, 95], thereby increasing the adoption of renewable energy across various industrial sectors. In Saemangeum, recruitment for 30MW-scale land-based solar power project operators is underway to accelerate RE100 [98, 102], and companies like Hanwha Q CELLS and POSCO are collaborating to promote agri-voltaic solar power systems [99, 101, 105], accelerating the construction of renewable energy infrastructure. However, there are warnings that renewable energy stocks are showing weakness [100], and despite an increase in renewable energy generation, coal power has also risen, leading to a 0.2% increase in greenhouse gas emissions from the power sector [96]. Furthermore, in some regions, movements counteracting the renewable energy transition are observed, such as the federal government easing climate change regulations for an Indiana power plant [107], presenting a complex challenge of expanding renewable energy while simultaneously ensuring stable energy security [34, 84, 90, 111].

sections.title: ⚠️ The Dual Nature of AI Technology Advancement and Climate Response
sections.content: Recently, at the world's largest climate event and UN meetings, Artificial Intelligence (AI) emerged as a key topic alongside war and climate change, putting international cooperation to the test [4, 112, 126]. Concerns have been raised about the surging power consumption of AI, but some analyses suggest that AI is not a primary emitter of global climate change [5]. Nevertheless, experts worry that AI could distract from the focus on climate response [4], and a significant portion of power applications for AI data centers have turned out to be speculative, raising fundamental questions about renewable energy supply [85]. However, there is also a growing call for AI to be actively utilized in addressing aging populations, care, and climate change [12]. Indeed, its potential as a climate solution is also gaining attention, with AI being used to demonstrate urban-level carbon neutrality [42] and strategic collaborations like 'AI × Carbon Literacy' exploring a major transition to carbon neutrality [44, 65]. The COP31 presidency emphasized the importance of responsible technology use by announcing an AI energy use pledge [119].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the comprehensive intensification of the climate crisis, alongside renewed recognition of the importance of technological advancement, energy transition efforts, and citizen participation. This is a critical juncture demanding sustained attention and action on climate change. This concludes today's climate briefing.
